kept.heading: THE HARMS OF SHORT-FORM VIDEO ON THE BRAIN ARE STARTING TO SHOW (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Heavy short-form video use may impair attention and memory. A meta-analysis of about 70 studies found stronger links to cognitive problems than mental health issues, with compulsive use predicting worse outcomes. Other research links more phone time to poorer working memory and uncontrolled short-form use to weaker episodic memory. Memory and imagination share neural circuitry, so these effects could also make it harder to envision and plan for the future.

kept.heading: HAS MAINSTREAM CULTURE DISAPPEARED? NEW YOUTUBE TRENDS RESEARCH SAYS NO (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Mainstream culture isn't disappearing, but brands can no longer rely on celebrities or broad media to create cultural relevance. YouTube creators and memes are now seen as widely known as Hollywood stars. Cultural momentum often starts in niche online communities before spreading through sharing and creating. YouTube says the platform can turn that momentum into broader cultural validation, with 65% of respondents saying something feels more real or legitimate when they see it there.

kept.heading: "PROOF OF HUMANITY" IS THE BIGGEST MARKETING OPPORTUNITY RIGHT NOW (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: 66% of people under 30 already react negatively when a business visibly uses AI in its ads, a reversal for the generation assumed to be AI's biggest fans. That backlash is turning restraint itself into a content opportunity, since publicly declaring what a brand won't automate can work as marketing in its own right, not just a compliance footnote. Aerie's pledge to skip AI-generated models became its most-liked Instagram post ever, with a 23% sales bump the same quarter.

kept.heading: ARE WE BUILDING BRANDS FOR A WORLD THAT NO LONGER EXISTS? (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Brands still rely on growth tactics built for a simpler, more stable world. This piece argues for a “both/and” approach. Keep evidence-based marketing principles while accounting for trust, context, and long-term consequences. Set rules against manipulative tactics. Use brand touchpoints to explain real-world decisions. Dedicate 10% of activity to retention, employee pride, and referrals.

kept.heading: THE NEW RULES OF GROWTH (WEBINAR)
kept.blurb: High-growth marketing teams are changing how they hire and allocate resources as growth demands rise. On September 17, Krithika Shankarraman of Thrive Capital and Christy Roach of AirOps will share how they secure resources, measure newer channels like AI Search, and get more leverage from smaller teams as growth accelerates.

kept.heading: WHAT IT ACTUALLY TAKES TO WIN ON REDDIT (WEBINAR)
kept.blurb: This session, on September 22, explores how brands can build a meaningful presence on Reddit. It covers subreddit culture, moderator relationships, and community engagement. Rachel Duffy shares how The Times built its Reddit strategy and drove visibility and trust. The session also looks at Reddit's role as search and LLMs reshape audience behavior.

kept.heading: DOES RETAIL MEDIA ADD VALUE? (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Retail media only adds value when ads drive profitable incremental sales. For advertisers, high ROAS can be misleading if shoppers would have purchased anyway. Retailers can also hurt margins if ads displace organic conversions or degrade the shopping experience. Both sides should measure whether advertising changes outcomes.

kept.heading: ARE YOU DOING MARKETING…OR BUILDING SOFTWARE? (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: 95% of enterprise GenAI projects show zero return. The biggest gap is in areas with strong off-the-shelf options, such as rank tracking, citation monitoring, and content scoring. Vendors serving thousands of customers have already solved these integration challenges. Custom workflows are harder to outsource, but buying proven expertise can still beat learning through trial and error.

kept.heading: 3 IN 4 AMERICANS USE PHONES WHILE WATCHING TV (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Broadcasters and advertisers now plan for TV and mobile as one viewing environment.

kept.heading: COMPANIES ARE HIRING EDITORS TO RUN THOUGHT LEADERSHIP AND MEASURING THEM ON PIPELINE (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Companies are hiring senior editors to run thought leadership and tying the function to revenue. Workato, for example, measures its program on win rates, deal velocity, and average sales price instead of content output. Research shows thought leadership can influence buying decisions and reach “hidden buyers” who rarely interact with sales. Recurring research and publishing can also build category authority over time. Owned media is becoming a permanent function with editorial leadership and a pipeline-focused scorecard.

kept.heading: GEN Z ROMANTICISED THE LIBRARY INTO RELEVANCE AGAIN (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Gen Z is driving a library revival through viral TikTok and Instagram content. Creators frame libraries as aesthetic, free places to study, work, and socialize. 67% report visiting public libraries, including many who are not active readers. The trend also ties into growing interest in physical books and digital detox. For libraries, social content can turn cultural relevance into real-world visits and stronger evidence for continued public funding.

kept.heading: DON'T USE QUESTIONS IN YOUR TITLES (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Use statement-based headlines instead of questions to increase engagement with marketing content. A Stanford study found that question titles generated 71.6% fewer comments and 12.6% fewer clicks across experiments and analyses of more than 22,000 news articles, 3 million academic articles, and 53,000 Reddit posts. Questions may perform worse because they signal uncertainty and provide less immediate information to readers. Test statement formats such as “X compared to Y” against question-based titles, then check that title changes don't hurt SEO.

kept.heading: STOP TRYING TO GO VIRAL. YOU NEED THE RIGHT 100 PEOPLE TO KNOW WHO YOU ARE FIRST (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Personal branding isn't a numbers game, it's a positioning game. Being known for one specific thing, not several, is what makes a name and a topic become inseparable in someone else's mind. The first time an idea gets posted, it's scrolled past. The fifth time, it starts to register, and by the twentieth repetition a name becomes the person others associate with that topic. That kind of association compounds into leverage long before any follower count does.

kept.heading: AI OVERVIEWS AND PAID SEARCH: WHEN TO FIGHT, INFLUENCE, OR GENERATE DEMAND (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI Overviews make it harder to use one bidding strategy across every search query, so marketers should classify terms by intent and AI visibility before allocating budget. High-intent terms belong in the “Fight” bucket, where paying for absolute top placement can still generate direct sales. Informational terms belong in “Influence”, where SEO and PPC should work together to earn citations and brand mentions in AI answers. Zero-click opportunities belong in “Generate Demand”, where budget should move to YouTube, Demand Gen, and content that builds demand before the eventual commercial search. In one B2B account, 83.3% of queries triggering AI answer blocks were informational, showing why reallocating budget across these buckets can matter more than simply adjusting bids.

kept.heading: SALESFORCE AND NVIDIA'S NEW REASONING MODEL IS EVERYTHING THE AI LABS SHOULD FEAR (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Koa answers a problem Salesforce couldn't solve without Nvidia, a reasoning model trained for sales and support work that never has to touch a customer's actual data. It was post-trained entirely on synthetic conversations, including simulated irate customers and negotiating sales reps, and its architecture is built to reach a token-efficient answer faster than a general-purpose frontier model would. Its own AI gateway can now route reasoning-heavy requests to Koa instead of paying frontier-lab rates for the same work.

kept.heading: DOES TV ACTUALLY SUCK NOW? (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Streaming didn't shrink television's quality - it multiplied its supply, turning a manageable weekly lineup into a catalog large enough to produce real decision fatigue. An audience now half-watching on a second screen while scrolling through that catalog is bound to feel worse about whatever it lands on, regardless of how well made it actually is. The fix is a shift in viewing habits, not a demand on the industry to make better shows.

kept.heading: THE JOB MARKET HAS BEEN CONTRACTING FOR 31 MONTHS (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: White-collar hiring has contracted for 31 months, with professional and technical roles shrinking despite stable overall employment. The bigger change is repeated headcount deferrals, leaving existing teams to absorb work indefinitely. Instead of waiting for hiring to recover, identify what you're actually paid for beyond your job title. Turn those skills into something clients or smaller companies would pay for. Build a small version while still employed, then review your progress in 6 months.

kept.heading: HUMANIST AI IN PRACTICE: A PUBLIC CONSULTATION ON OUR CODE OF CONDUCT FOR MAI MODELS (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Microsoft published a first draft of its AI training and deployment manual.

kept.heading: AI AND GOOGLE UPDATES TO KNOW (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Google is reducing publishers' opportunities to earn search traffic as AI features take up more space. New sports features bring play-by-play updates and fantasy recommendations directly into Search. OpenAI is reportedly restricting some competitor ads in ChatGPT. Meanwhile, 41 of the 50 biggest US news sites saw traffic decline year over year. Several publishers have linked traffic losses to AI Overviews and AI Mode, while some are responding by investing more in direct audiences and reducing reliance on search.

kept.heading: WHY ACTIVITY WINS CUSTOMER ENGAGEMENT (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Traditional ads are losing attention as consumers tune out repetitive, sales-heavy formats. 88% of Gen Z and millennials ignore most ads, while 85% stay loyal to brands that feel genuine. Activity-based campaigns offer a different approach by motivating people to participate rather than simply buy. 65% of consumers say they're more likely to engage with or purchase from brands that motivate people to get active.

kept.heading: THE NEW YOUTUBE OPPORTUNITY FOR AGENCIES (WEBINAR)
kept.blurb: Agency leaders will discuss some of the newest ways that YouTube can make a brand and their agency successful on YouTube. They'll cover new ad formats and strategies, measurement tactics, and ways to tie advertising campaigns into other YouTube efforts from the brand, including organic and creator initiatives. The free webinar takes place today at 10 AM PT.

kept.heading: META ONE BUNDLES CREATOR AND BUSINESS TOOLS — FOR A MONTHLY FEE (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Meta's new subscription service prices creator and business tools from $2.99 a month for basic app access up to $499 for its top professional tier, with the $49.99 Advanced plan unlocking year-ahead scheduling, bulk uploads, and shared account access without password sharing. Paid tiers also boost visibility directly, through higher search placement and more prominent follow buttons, not just productivity tools. The core apps and Meta AI stay free, and none of the tiers remove ads.

kept.heading: THE DATA CENTER WATER MYTH (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Americans are increasingly hearing that AI data centers are draining the country's water supply, but the national scale of the problem is far smaller than viral claims suggest. US data centers consumed about 228 billion gallons of water in 2023, yet that amounted to only 0.015% to 0.2% of total US water withdrawals, compared with 43% for agriculture. A viral claim that every ChatGPT question consumes a bottle of water also misrepresented research that estimated 500 milliliters could be consumed across roughly 10 to 50 GPT -3 responses. Water use can still create serious local concerns, but misinformation and misleading comparisons are turning a site-specific resource issue into a broader narrative about AI infrastructure threatening the US water supply.

kept.heading: GRAPHIC DESIGNER ≠ ART DIRECTOR ≠ CREATIVE DIRECTOR (12 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Job title confusion runs in both directions. Companies without a creative background borrow a senior-sounding title off a template instead of defining the actual work, while designers themselves inflate titles because freelance clients rarely check credentials. Underneath the confusion, the jobs barely move: a designer executes one piece of visual communication, an art director keeps a whole project's output feeling like one brand, and a creative director sets the point of view behind it. Only company size decides how many people that work gets split across.

kept.heading: INSIDE THE CREATOR ECONOMY'S AI RECKONING (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Creator-economy sentiment toward AI has shifted in about a year from dread to a hunt for leverage, with most creators now treating AI output as a rough starting draft rather than a finished product. That shift is showing up in contracts: some brands now ask for access to creators' AI prompts, while creators are starting to write their own AI-use clauses back to protect their voice. Adoption itself splits by gender, since women are 22% less likely than men to be regular AI users at work and more likely to worry it looks like cutting corners. The recurring conclusion is that audiences still connect to the person behind the work, not the tool that helped make it.

kept.heading: PERPLEXITY IS TURNING CREATOR MARKETING INTO A PRODUCT TEST (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Rather than talking up the brand, creators would review original builds made in Perplexity's own tools, instead of promoting them.

kept.heading: HOW MUCH DOES A B2B CONTENT WRITER COST IN 2026 (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: A guide to how much B2B freelancers are charging in the UK.

kept.heading: ECONOMISTS CONCERNED THE AI BUBBLE IS ABOUT TO BLOW (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Equity and debt issuance are surging, market value is concentrated in a few major tech stocks, and earnings expectations look increasingly unstable.
